'''Sinaugoro''' is an Austronesian language of [[Papua New Guinea]]. It is mainly spoken in the [[Rigo District]] of [[Central Province (Papua New Guinea)|Central Province]] by some 15,000 people.<ref>{{harvp|Tauberschmidt|1999|page=1}}</ref> The language is closely related to [[Motu language|Motu]].

==Grammar==
Sinaugoro is an [[agglutinative]] language with ergative alignment and [[subject–object–verb]] (SOV) word order.<ref>{{harvp|Tauberschmidt|1999|page=2}}</ref>
Number is marked explicitly on the verb and freely within the noun phrase, but is not marked on the noun itself.  
A morphological distinction is made in Sinaugoro between the possession of alienable and inalienable nouns, and then between the alienable possession of edible and inedible objects.<ref>{{harvp|Tauberschmidt|1999|page=14}}</ref>

Verbal indexing of person and number in Sinaugoro makes freestanding personal pronouns optional. These are given below, displaying a distinction between inclusive and exclusive.
